statement: Let r be the returned vector. Define a sequence o and times t_k as follows. Set t_0 = 0. For k = 0,1,...,n-1, let R_k be the set of labels i with 0 <= i < n that do not occur among o[0],...,o[k-1]. Let a_k = t_k if there exists i in R_k with e_i <= t_k; otherwise let a_k = min_{i in R_k} e_i. Let o[k] be the unique i in R_k with e_i <= a_k such that for every j in R_k with e_j <= a_k, either p_i < p_j, or p_i = p_j and i <= j. Set t_{k+1} = a_k + p_{o[k]}. Then len(r) = n and r[k] = o[k] for every k with 0 <= k < n. Thus r is exactly the order in which the CPU processes the tasks, including idle jumps to the next enqueue time when no remaining task is available.
preconditions: Let n = len(tasks). For every i with 0 <= i < n, len(tasks[i]) = 2; write e_i = tasks[i][0] and p_i = tasks[i][1]. Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= e_i, p_i <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

preconditions: Let n = len(tasks). For every i with 0 <= i < n, len(tasks[i]) = 2; write e_i = tasks[i][0] and p_i = tasks[i][1]. Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= e_i, p_i <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r that is a permutation of 0..n-1, define s_0 = min_{0<=i<n} e_i and, for 0 <= k < n-1, s_{k+1} = max(s_k + p_{r[k]}, e_{r[k+1]}). Then for every k with 0 <= k < n, s_k >= e_{r[k]}. In particular, s_0 = e_{r[0]} = min_i e_i, so the first processed task has the minimum enqueue time.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r that is a permutation of 0..n-1, define s_0 = min_i e_i and s_{k+1} = max(s_k + p_{r[k]}, e_{r[k+1]}) for 0 <= k < n-1. For 0 <= k <= n let R_k = {i | 0 <= i < n and i does not occur among r[0],...,r[k-1]}. Then for every k with 0 <= k < n, r[k] is in R_k, e_{r[k]} <= s_k, and for every j in R_k with e_j <= s_k, either p_{r[k]} < p_j, or p_{r[k]} = p_j and r[k] <= j.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r that is a permutation of 0..n-1, define s_0 = min_i e_i, f_k = s_k + p_{r[k]}, and s_{k+1} = max(f_k, e_{r[k+1]}) for 0 <= k < n-1. For 0 <= k < n let R_{k+1} = {i | 0 <= i < n and i does not occur among r[0],...,r[k]}. Then for every k with 0 <= k < n-1: if there exists j in R_{k+1} with e_j <= f_k, then s_{k+1} = f_k; if no j in R_{k+1} has e_j <= f_k, then s_{k+1} = e_{r[k+1]} and e_{r[k+1]} > f_k.

For any two distinct labels i,j with 0 <= i,j < n, if e_i > e_j and (p_i < p_j or (p_i = p_j and i < j)), and if j occurs before i in r, then the start time of j is strictly less than e_i: if r[v] = j, then s_v < e_i.

statement: Let tasks' be the input array with tasks'[i][0] = e_i + c and tasks'[i][1] = p_i for all i. Then get_order(tasks') = get_order(tasks): adding the same constant c to every enqueue time leaves the returned processing order unchanged.
preconditions: Let n = len(tasks). For every i with 0 <= i < n, len(tasks[i]) = 2; write e_i = tasks[i][0] and p_i = tasks[i][1]. Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= e_i, p_i <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n. Let c be an integer with c >= 0 and (max_{0<=i<n} e_i) + c <= 1000000000.
